clue.text: Dogs, are warmed and dried and given drinks

parts.note: linen is aired when warmed and dried out in an airing cupboard
ales are beers, drinks in a pub

explanation.surface: Some pampered pets are warmed through, towelled dry and given something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Airedales are a breed of large terrier, so they are dogs.

explanation.surface: A fondness that is really an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are real: fondness or warm attachment, and an old medical term for a bodily complaint, as in 'an affection of the lungs'.

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are only loosely in order and must be rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A holiday keepsake bought for about a hundred Italian lire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like it qualifies the price, but it signals an anagram of LIRE, giving RELI, before the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something kept in memory of the past, much as a keepsake is.

explanation.surface: A strong player overhits in a ball game and is then expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a player who hits too hard sends the ball beyond the lines of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive hit too hard leaves the court in a ball game, and to banish someone is to expel them by force.

parts.note: the fictional murderous London barber would soap a customer's face before shaving, and a word for thrashed also means soaped up

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed by the demon barber of Fleet Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the murderous barber of Victorian melodrama; 'beaten' suggests violence, but the barber's real work is foaming up the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both thrashed and covered in soap foam, which is what a barber does before a shave.

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for reels is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: reels of thread or film are spools

explanation.surface: Fishing reels appear on board some boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses SPOOLS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloops are single-masted sailing vessels, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Girl makes trouble — little time to return

indicators.note: to return says the pieces for trouble and a short time are read backwards

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado
hr is the short form of hour, a little piece of time

explanation.surface: A girl causes a fuss and then has to come back shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns ADOHR round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female first name.

explanation.surface: A choice between striking back and giving in.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow can be paid back in kind, and an investment's profit is its income.

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and changed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Musicians are served a dish of cooked carrots, much to their surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' tells you to rearrange CARROTS and EH.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of instrumental musicians.

clue.text: English king misses church in French city

indicators.note: misses says the king's name goes without the letters for church

parts.note: Charles was the name of two Stuart kings of England

explanation.surface: A king of England skips church while in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' removes CH from CHARLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Arles is a city in Provence in southern France.

explanation.surface: Something comes about and leads to an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to pass is an old sense of the phrasal verb, and two friends who argue and stop speaking have done the same.

clue.text: Concerned with seeing the Capitol, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests a different arrangement of the building's name is the one wanted

explanation.surface: A sightseeing visit to the Washington building, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of CAPITOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight or vision.

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: Revolutionary leader Che Guevara keeps a hidden supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden hoard of goods or weapons.

parts.note: ex means former, what something had been
porters carry luggage

explanation.surface: Traders who used to work hauling bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's first syllable as the prefix for 'former': former porters.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchants who send goods abroad for sale are traders in the overseas market.

clue.text: Comprises batting hints about five hundred

parts.note: a cricket side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: about says the word for hints goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: clues are hints to a solution
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman's tips, covering about five hundred runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting' is the cricket sense: a side at the crease is 'in'. 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise something is to contain it as part of the whole.

clue.text: An ice in the feature film, perhaps ?

definitions.text: An ice in the feature film, perhaps

parts.words: An ice in the feature film, perhaps
parts.note: the feature is a facial feature, the film a thin layer, and the ice a chilly kind of dessert cream

explanation.surface: A frozen dessert eaten in the main movie at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature film' suggests the cinema; read it as a thin layer spread on the face, a cool cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is a soothing cosmetic smoothed onto the face, a chilly cream rather than a dessert.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dish that some diners sample cautiously.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is a dish of meat and vegetables slowly simmered.

clue.text: About to back "car into power unit -corporation vehicle

indicators.note: into says the inner pieces are placed inside the unit of power

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power

indicators.note: to back says the short word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A council truck reversing a car into an electrical unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns RE into ER; ER and CAR go 'into' WATT. The corporation is a town council, whose cart once sprinkled the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A water cart is a wagon carrying water, used by town councils for street-cleaning.

clue.text: Capital wrinkle found in the paper

parts.note: head means the top or capital, as a capital tops a column
a line is a crease or wrinkle in the skin

explanation.surface: A city wrinkle that turns up in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' wants to be a city; here it is the head, the top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the title in large type above a newspaper story.

indicators.note: members treats the letters of the word as the parts that make it up, to be gathered in any order

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A scold reprimands the club members over their morning gin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'members' of CHIDES are its letters, which rearrange into SCHIED; 'taking' adds AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Schiedam is a Dutch gin, named after the distilling town near Rotterdam.

parts.note: the letter O looks like the figure nought, which is nil

explanation.surface: An Old English scribe seen beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O.E.' looks like the abbreviation for Old English; read the O as nought, NIL, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of Egypt.

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone shows a leaning towards writing and singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or tendency.

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
limousines are large cars

explanation.surface: Prizes given for enormous chauffeured cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Outsize cars are huge limousines; the Oscars are the Hollywood film awards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the annual Academy film prizes.

clue.text: Wind or wave, as it appears

parts.note: a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A gust or a swell, by the look of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind or wave' looks like a choice; 'Wind' is the definition and 'wave' gives BORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreas is the Greek god of the north wind, and the name stands for that wind.

clue.text: Defenders promise to supply a weapon

parts.note: backs are defensive players in football
giving one's word is promising

explanation.surface: Defending players pledge to hand over arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A backsword is a sword with one sharp edge.

explanation.surface: Something to eat for those in commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals provided, as in bed and board, and the directors who run a company.

parts.note: Samuel Johnson wrote a series of essays under a title meaning a lazy person, which also reads as an adjective for less active

explanation.surface: The lazier of Dr Johnson's writings.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson, the dictionary maker, also wrote a weekly essay series in the 1750s whose title doubles as 'more lazy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is Johnson's essay series and also the comparative of a word for lazy.

clue.text: Everyone is upset over refusal, that's plain

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue, upset means the word for everyone is turned upside down

parts.note: all means everyone
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Everyone is distressed by a rejection, that's clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALL into LLA, set 'over' NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy treeless plain in South America.

clue.text: A girl gets half — that's mean !

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

indicators.note: half says take the first half of the word, two letters out of four

explanation.surface: A girl receives only half, and complains that is stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' here is the arithmetic sense, not stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: An average is a mean value in arithmetic.

parts.note: a native American was called an Indian
capital means first-rate, as A is first-rate in A1

explanation.surface: A country's original inhabitants and their chief city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city; here it means excellent, A as in A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: These coins' returned with old halfpenny

indicators.note: returned means the letters for an old halfpenny are written backwards

parts.note: half is semi and an old penny is d, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: Some coins come back together with a pre-decimal halfpenny.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pre-1971 money D stood for a penny; SEMI (half) plus D, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimes are American ten-cent coins.

clue.text: A mast to be adapted for the vessel

indicators.note: adapted says the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ship's mast is to be modified to suit the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' signals an anagram of A MAST TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat is a boat powered by a steam engine.
